note: Things to take up rather than attend once — a studio, a choir, a book group, a garden, a table of chess. Hand-researched: every record was checked against the organisation's own page on `lastVerified`, and none of them is sport, which has its own tab. `rhythm` is how often it runs (weekly, monthly, anytime, occasional); `commitment` is what it asks of you to start (dropin, book, term, member); `firstStep` says how to begin in the organisation's own terms. Read by the Regulars tab in js/app.js.

items.title: Sunday bird walks at the Delhi Zoo
items.times: Every Sunday, 6.30am to 9.30am; report at the entrance by 6.15am. Twenty places a week, 18 and over
items.firstStep: Register Monday to Friday through the zoo’s website or the NZP Sathi app
items.area: National Zoological Park, off Mathura Road
items.why: The zoo sits beside Purana Qila, and on Sunday mornings a guide takes twenty people round them before the gates open to everyone else. It is free, and with places going first-come each week, registering on Monday becomes part of the ritual.
items.hoursNote: Every Sunday, 6.30am to 9.30am; report at the entrance by 6.15am. Twenty places a week, 18 and over

items.title: Classes at Triveni Kala Sangam
items.times: Painting, drawing, sculpture, glass art and photography; Bharatanatyam, Odissi, Manipuri and Chhau; Hindustani vocal, sitar, flute and tabla
items.firstStep: Art classes begin with an interview with the head of department — call the office to arrange it
items.area: 205 Tansen Marg, between Mandi House and Bengali Market
items.priceNote: Monthly tuition, plus one month’s fee as a refundable deposit
items.why: Since 1950 this low modernist building near Mandi House has been where Delhi goes to learn an art properly: painting and sculpture, classical dance, Hindustani music, photography. Classes meet three times a week, so it is a real commitment — and between them you have the galleries, the open-air sculpture court and the terrace café, which is the other reason to keep coming back.
items.hoursNote: Painting, drawing, sculpture, glass art and photography; Bharatanatyam, Odissi, Manipuri and Chhau; Hindustani vocal, sitar, flute and tabla

items.title: Gandharva Mahavidyalaya
items.cadence: Weekly classes through the academic year
items.times: Hindustani vocal and instrumental music and classical dance; separate vocal classes for men and women
items.firstStep: A short audition — prepare a one-minute song of any kind
items.priceNote: Term fees — see the admissions page
items.why: A music school founded in 1939 in the Gwalior gharana tradition, open to anybody from eleven upward whatever their background. The audition is gentle — a one-minute song, classical, film or folk — and after it you are learning raga the traditional way, in a room with a teacher, week after week.
items.hoursNote: Hindustani vocal and instrumental music and classical dance; separate vocal classes for men and women

items.title: French at the Alliance Française de Delhi
items.times: Six levels from A1 to C2, in seasonal sessions; the autumn 2026 session is under way
items.firstStep: Beginners join at the start of a session; others take a placement test
items.why: French taught level by level in a building on the edge of the Lodhi Garden, with the city’s largest French library — thirty thousand books — upstairs. A session is weeks of classes with the same small group, which is what makes it stick.
items.hoursNote: Six levels from A1 to C2, in seasonal sessions; the autumn 2026 session is under way

items.title: Weekend walks with Delhi Heritage Walks
items.cadence: Weekends, a different quarter each time
items.times: Public walks on weekends through the lesser-known corners of the city — Chandni Chowk, Hauz Khas, Lodhi Garden and more
items.firstStep: Book a place on the next public walk online
items.area: Meets in a different part of Delhi each weekend
items.why: A group of young historians who spend their weekends walking small groups through the parts of Delhi guidebooks skip. Each walk is a different chapter — a stepwell, a Sufi shrine, a Mughal lane — so a season of them adds up to knowing the city properly. Book the next one when you finish the last.
items.hoursNote: Public walks on weekends through the lesser-known corners of the city — Chandni Chowk, Hauz Khas, Lodhi Garden and more

items.title: Delhi Book Lovers
items.cadence: Monthly, on the third or fourth weekend
items.times: A book or a theme of the month, discussed in person on the third or fourth weekend
items.firstStep: Join the group on Meetup and RSVP for the next meeting
items.why: One of the biggest book clubs in Delhi NCR, with more than three thousand members, meeting once a month to talk about a chosen book or theme. With that many people it never feels like joining somebody else’s circle of friends — you RSVP, you turn up, and the conversation carries you.
items.hoursNote: A book or a theme of the month, discussed in person on the third or fourth weekend

items.title: The IHC Free Book X'Change
items.times: On one Sunday a month, 11am to 4pm, near the IHC information centre — check the Habitat calendar for the date
items.firstStep: Bring books you have finished; take away up to two
items.source: India Habitat Centre — Habitat World calendar
items.why: A book flea market where nothing costs anything: bring the books you no longer have room for, browse everyone else’s, and leave with two. It is as much an adda as a swap — people come for the talk about what to read next and stay for lunch at the Habitat.
items.hoursNote: On one Sunday a month, 11am to 4pm, near the IHC information centre — check the Habitat calendar for the date

items.title: Pottery at the Delhi Blue Pottery Trust
items.cadence: Weekend classes, most of the year
items.times: A six-month basic course on weekends — throwing, lids and handles, slab work, firing and glazing — all year except 1 December to 15 January; two- to three-hour blue-pottery workshops too
items.firstStep: Try a two-hour blue-pottery workshop, then sign up for the six-month course
items.area: Lado Sarai art district, near Mehrauli
items.priceNote: Course and workshop fees on enquiry
items.why: A small studio and gallery in the Lado Sarai art district that teaches both halves of the craft: a proper six-month weekend course in the wheel and the kiln, and the Jaipur blue-pottery technique made from quartz, glass and multani mitti rather than clay. Weekend classes run all year except the coldest six weeks.
items.hoursNote: A six-month basic course on weekends — throwing, lids and handles, slab work, firing and glazing — all year except 1 December to 15 January; two- to three-hour blue-pottery workshops too

items.title: Naveen Chhaya pottery studio
items.firstStep: Book a single 90-minute session (₹1,500) before committing to a course
items.why: A working studio in the lanes of Hauz Khas, run by two artists, with the wheel, hand-building, slab work, sculpture and glazing all on offer. You can pay by the session to find out whether you like it, then move to a month of eight or twelve classes, or a weekend-only course if weekdays are impossible.

items.title: Delhi Chess Club
items.firstStep: Take a monthly membership — day passes are promised
items.area: H-1/1B Model Town III, near Azadpur Metro
items.priceNote: Monthly or yearly membership, coffee and snacks included
items.why: A relaxed weekend chess room in North Delhi, near the university, with more than five hundred members, weekly tournaments with prizes, strategy workshops and unlimited coffee in the fee. It is open to every level and every age, which is exactly what a chess habit needs: somebody at your level every time you come back.

items.title: Volunteering with Goonj
items.firstStep: Sign up on the volunteer page, or call the Sarita Vihar centre
items.why: The nonprofit that turns the city’s unused clothes and household things into material for villages across India, run from a centre in Sarita Vihar. Volunteers sort and pack, run collection drives, lead readings or bring whatever skill they have. A regular Saturday there is some of the most tangible good you can do in Delhi.
